To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) mitochondrial energy dysfunction and oxidative damage to mitochondrial and nuclear DNA are associated with the pathogenesis of HD and other neurodegenerative disease; 2) oxidative damage and mitochondrial dysfunction are linked to excitotoxic mechanisms of cell death in neurons; 3) the molecular defects underlying neurodegenerative processes are associated with increased sensitivity to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction; 4) the molecular defects are associated with increased susceptibility to excitotoxicity; 5) mitochondrial dysfunction and excitotoxicity
Oxidative damage to mitochondrial DNA, proteins and lipids is a prominent feature of chronic neurodegeneration in humans and experimental animals.

1) oxidative damage to mitochondrial and nuclear DNA and other macromolecules is a common feature in all neurodegenerative disease; 2) oxidative stress may be an important cause of mitochondrial DNA damage and dysfunction; 3) mitochondrial DNA damage and mitochondrial dysfunction may play an intrinsic role in the pathogenesis and/or pathophysiology of these diseases; and 4) the mitochondrial energy dysfunction may lead to neuronal death through an excitotoxic mechanism.

elucidating mechanisms whereby molecular defects in neurodegenerativerelated genes can lead to the progressive degeneration of neurons.
the role of free radical-mediated oxidative damage in the pathogenesis and progression of neurodegenerativediseases, with a focus on mitochondrial dysfunction and excitotoxic mechanisms.
the role of mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative damage in the pathogenesis, and possible treatment of neurodegenera- tive disorders.
